results.title: Outcome taxonomy and agent timestamps
results.summary: Added nullable limit_hit/error_kind/agent_started_at/agent_finished_at columns (schema + additive repair with a type-guarded read), StageFailure/inStage error-kind classification on the host and container paths (including the container IIFE catch), graded timeouts on both paths (container export guard returns incomplete), agent-phase timestamps, the four export fields, error-kind and limit badges in Matrix and Attempt, a seeded graded-timeout cell, regenerated dev-data, the new tests/outcome-taxonomy.test.ts, updated runner and docker timeout tests, and doc updates. typecheck, lint, the spec test set (72 pass), genericity, ui:build and ui:e2e (30 pass) all pass; full bun test has 1 failure that predates this phase (mcp auth credentials-file test, which also fails with the changes stashed). The dev-data git-clean check can only pass once dev-data is committed: regeneration is byte-identical across runs, and all of ui/dev-data (including new untracked snapshots/ dirs from drift already present at HEAD) must be committed. Docker-gated test edits were not run locally because no daemon is available. — The implementation matches the Phase 1 spec closely. It adds four nullable columns with duplicate-column-safe repairs and a type guard on read, grades timeouts on both host and container paths with the export-failure guard falling back to `incomplete`, tags errors by stage via `StageFailure`/`inStage` so helpers don't need to know about error kinds, and maps them to `run.json` without bumping `DATA_SCHEMA_VERSION`. The UI badges, seeders, e2e assertions and the matrix's incomplete-reason split all fit together, and outcome-taxonomy.test.ts covers every case the spec names. There are no critical or high findings, so it is ready to commit. The four low findings are optional cleanups.
findings: low/logic scripts/seed-run.ts:434 — The seeded `error` outcome now has `errorKind: "agent"`, but its message is still "attempt timed out after 1500000ms". Under the new rules a timeout is a graded completed attempt, not an error, so the dev data and the e2e error-kind drill-down contradict the model the phase introduces. → Change the seeded error message to an agent-failure message such as "agent command exited 1", then run `bun run ui:dev-data` again.

low/testing tests/outcome-taxonomy.test.ts:"an unpreparable local/ starting state → environment" — The spec asked for a `localDir` pointing at a missing path. The test locks a `node_modules` directory with chmod 000 instead and skips itself under uid 0, so a CI job running as root never checks the `environment` classification. → Add a comment explaining why a missing path cannot be used (discovery or the identity hash rejects it first), or add a second case that works for root, e.g. a `localDir` swapped to a missing path after discovery.

low/testing src/runner/execute.ts:922-928 — The container-path guard (export fails after a timeout → `incomplete`, `limit_hit` still recorded) is not tested anywhere, including the Docker-gated suites. → Add a Docker-gated case in tests/docker.test.ts, or a note in the test file that this branch is covered only by manual review.

low/spec-deviation docs/extensions.md:47, docs/publishing-a-benchmark.md:195-200 — Both docs changed but are not in the spec's File Changes. The edits are correct and needed now that timeouts are graded, but extensions.md:47 is one very long line, unlike the ~80-column wrapping around it. → Keep the edits and wrap extensions.md:47 to match the surrounding lines.

results.title: Graded checks and SDK recall
results.summary: Added optional CheckResult.graded (validated as boolean), per-name graded tally and per-experiment SDK recall (collectRecall) in the report with REPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION 6->7, a methodology sentence and text-renderer line, a stale-schema rebuild in resolveReport (reuses stored pricing), UI ungraded tag + graded-only matrix counts + SDK recall card, seeded ungraded sdk-wired check, docs, and tests/graded-checks.test.ts. Every validation command passes, and the full suite has 348 pass and 1 fail. That one failure is an env-dependent MCP credential test that also fails on HEAD. The dev-data drift check was verified by regenerating twice and diffing the trees, since the literal git-diff form cannot pass while changes must stay unstaged. Unrequested but logged in the notes: ungraded checks are also filtered out of diagnose failedChecks. — PASS with 0 blocking findings: the implementation matches the phase-2 spec. `graded` is added to the type and validator, the report tallies it per check name, collectRecall handles the null-rate case and is wired into collectExperiments, REPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION goes from 6 to 7, and resolveReport rebuilds a stale-schema report before the verbatim-reuse branch. The seeder, docs, UI tags, graded-only matrix counts and e2e checks all follow the spec, and tests/graded-checks.test.ts covers everything the spec asks for, including the end-to-end runner invariant. The remaining findings are one misplaced doc comment, two small documented deviations and one missing edge-case test. None of them blocks the commit.
findings: medium/pattern-mismatch src/report/report.ts:365 — The new collectRecall JSDoc was inserted between collectExperiments' existing doc comment ("Identity cards from the manifest, verbatim...") and the function it describes. That leaves two JSDoc blocks stacked above collectRecall, and collectExperiments at :386 now has no doc comment. → Move the "Identity cards..." comment down so it sits directly above `function collectExperiments(run, attempts)`, and keep only the SDK-recall comment above collectRecall.

low/spec-deviation src/report/report.ts:317 — The spec defines `sdk_recall: ReportRecall` as required on ReportExperiment. The code makes it optional (`sdk_recall?:`), citing schema < 7 artifacts. The reason holds for immutable hosted snapshots, and the UI and text renderer both handle a missing value. → Keep it optional, but note the deviation in the phase notes so later phases know readers must handle a missing value. Or make it required and narrow the optionality to the UI's reader type.

low/spec-deviation src/diagnose/select.ts:103 — This file is not in the spec's File Changes. failedChecks now leaves out ungraded checks. The change is sensible (ungraded misses are not failures) and tests/graded-checks.test.ts:154 covers it. → Keep it, and add a line for src/diagnose/select.ts to the spec's Modified Files table so the change is on record.

low/testing tests/graded-checks.test.ts:161 — The stale-schema rebuild test covers only a stored report without cost_estimate. The failure-mode row about reusing `stored.cost_estimate.pricing` when rebuilding (src/export.ts:261) has no test. → Add a case that writes a schema-6 report with a cost_estimate.pricing snapshot and asserts the exported report keeps a cost_estimate built from that pricing.

results.title: Oracle adapter, solution/ convention, validate --oracle
results.summary:
Built three pieces. (1) Discovery now finds solution/ per eval, or solution/<fw>/ for framework evals, and records its tree hash on EvalIdentity.solution outside components. (2) A built-in oracle adapter (host and container) with startingState "solution": the shared prepWorkspaceSource (moved to src/runner/workspace-source.ts) overlays solution/ on local/, and run preflight refuses oracle pairs whose eval has no solution. (3) `validate --oracle` prints 1.0/deferred/FAILED/MISSING per eval using a capability-tracking context, and exits 1 on any FAILED or MISSING. All spec validation commands pass (the Docker-gated container test was skipped because no daemon was running). Deviations are logged in implementation notes:
- The oracle fixture experiment lives at tests/__fixtures__/oracle/experiments/.
- validateOracle works per eval.
- RuntimeCapabilityError is not exported, because the class cannot cross the worker boundary.

Caution for the commit stage: scripts/seed-run.ts also holds uncommitted edits from a concurrent sibling phase. Mine is only `solution: null` on the EvalIdentity literal. The sibling's other uncommitted work (diagnose, ui, docs/concepts.md, seed-site) is not in this list. One full-suite failure, in mcp-proxy.test.ts, comes from the missing Docker daemon and also fails on HEAD. — Phase 4 matches the spec closely: solution/ discovery with the per-framework error, `solution` recorded outside `components`, the shared `prepWorkspaceSource` overlay keyed off `startingState`, no-op host and container oracle adapters registered on both paths, a preflight that runs before any run row and names every pair, and `validate --oracle` with capability tracking on the parent side of the worker plus all the specified outcome lines. There are no critical or high findings. The one medium item is that editing only solution/ changes the run-manifest hash and so blocks `--resume`. The rest are small notes-or-tests gaps, so it is ready to commit. Review was static only: under the Bash-for-git-only rule I did not run tests, typecheck, lint or the CLI. The working tree also holds phase-6 changes (diagnose clusters, UI, docs/concepts.md), which were not reviewed here and should be committed separately from phase 4.
findings: medium/logic src/manifest.ts:175 — `solution` sits outside `components`, so the eval hash and pair identity are unchanged, as the spec requires. But it is still inside the RunManifest object that `contentHash(withoutHash)` hashes, so `manifest.hash` changes when only solution/ is edited. The resume check at src/runner/execute.ts:464 compares that hash, so `--resume` of an ordinary non-oracle run is refused after a solution-only edit, even though agents never see solution/. → Pick one of two fixes. (a) Keep this behaviour and add a sentence to docs/writing-an-eval.md saying that editing solution/ mid-run blocks `--resume`. (b) Leave `solution` out of the object passed to the manifest-hash computation, and add a test showing that a solution-only edit does not change `manifest.hash`.

low/spec-deviation tests/__fixtures__/oracle/experiments/oracle-local.ts:1 — The spec puts this fixture at tests/__fixtures__/experiments/oracle-local.ts. The builder moved it under oracle/, which looks deliberate: tests/cli.test.ts:50,67 validate that shared experiments root, and a new module there would change their output. → Keep the new location and record the move in implementation-notes-phase-4 so the spec and the code agree.

low/spec-deviation src/index.ts — `RuntimeCapabilityError` is not exported. The spec made this conditional, and the class doc at src/runner/context.ts:71-77 explains why: the class does not survive the scorer-worker boundary, so scorers could not catch it by type anyway. → Record this decision in the phase notes. If you do export it, add a doc comment saying scorers must match on the message, not use instanceof.

low/testing tests/oracle.test.ts:76 — The spec asks for two evals that are identical except for solution/, with equal `hash` and different `solution`. The first identity test uses two differently named evals, so it can only compare `local` and `scorer`. The case of adding or removing solution/ is only implied by the edit test. → Add one assertion: build the manifest, `rmSync` the eval's solution/, rebuild, then assert `hash` is equal and `solution` is null.

low/testing tests/oracle.test.ts:222 — The Docker case uses bare `alpine:3`, which has no git, so the container git baseline is skipped. That leaves untested the spec's claim that the overlay runs before the baseline commit, which keeps the container oracle diff empty. It also only asserts a pass. → Use the git-enabled test image pattern from tests/docker.test.ts:57-59 and assert that the attempt's diff is empty.

results.title: Report honesty
results.summary:
Built all three Phase 6 changes. (1) Transcript excerpts now anchor on the last cluster of error markers, and DIAGNOSIS_PROMPT_VERSION is bumped to 2. (2) Compare shows a `compare-n-notice` when a run has fewer than 3 trials, or when a shared eval has an arm with nothing scored. (3) Diagnosis now groups findings into `diagnosis-cluster` sections keyed by (eval, failing graded checks), joined from report.json, and `eval-defect` leads when it is at least 25% of findings. Supporting changes: a new pure helper `ui/src/diagnosis-clusters.ts` plus `tests/diagnose-clusters.test.ts`; a third seeded trials-1 run (new `idSalt` and `startedAt` seed options, dated older so the sweep stays the default run); e2e and docs updates; regenerated dev-data. Validation: typecheck, lint, the three spec test files, genericity, ui:build and all 32 e2e tests pass. The spec's `git diff --quiet -- ui/dev-data` check cannot pass while the regenerated data is unstaged, so I checked that regeneration is deterministic instead (two regenerations match byte for byte). Watch for:
- A sibling phase has uncommitted changes in the same working tree (src/manifest.ts adds a `solution` field), and the regenerated dev-data picks it up. Re-run `bun run ui:dev-data` once both phases land.
- 2 tests fail in the full suite (mcp-proxy and container preflight): mcp-proxy fails on the unreachable Docker socket, and neither touches this phase's files.
Six decisions are logged in implementation-notes-phase-6.html. — Phase 6 matches the spec. Excerpt anchoring follows the spec's snippet exactly, and the 5 excerpt test expectations match hand calculation. DIAGNOSIS_PROMPT_VERSION is 2, clusterFindings and targetOrder match the spec's interface and ordering rules, and the Diagnosis view gates on the report with a null fallback. The Compare notice works: absent on the sweep run, present with 'this run: 1' on the new seeded trials-1 run. I checked this against the seeded report and dev-data. The only real gap is that the 'arm with nothing scored' branch of the notice is untested, so it's ready to commit, ideally after adding those unit tests. I read the code but did not run any tests or builds.
findings: medium/testing ui/src/views/Compare.tsx:nNoticeSentences — Nothing tests the second notice sentence ('Some shared evals have an arm with nothing scored…'). Nothing tests the shared-eval narrowing either (every member must have attempted the eval). No unit test covers them, and no seeded run triggers them: the cell-states and n1 runs have no empty arm. The narrowing matters: without it, the sweep's regression eval callback-redirect-loop (run only by claude-docs and codex-docs) would show the notice on the sweep run, against the spec's 'absent on the sweep run'. → Move nNoticeSentences, countArms and attemptedArms into a pure ui module, following the ui/src/diagnosis-clusters.ts pattern. Then add unit tests for four cases: an arm whose attempts all errored in a shared eval triggers the sentence; an eval only one member ran does not; withheld or singleton-only groups return []; trials < 3 plus an empty arm yields both sentences.

low/spec-deviation ui/src/views/Compare.tsx:79-96 — The spec's condition is 'any compared group has an eval where some arm has scored === 0'. The code narrows this to evals that every member attempted. The narrowing is justified (see the testing finding) and the doc comment documents it, but it departs from the spec's wording. → Keep the behavior. Add one clause to the Compare n-notice paragraph in docs/concepts.md saying that evals run by only some arms do not trigger the notice, so docs match the code.

low/pattern-mismatch ui/src/views/Diagnosis.tsx:215 — Each cluster now emits the nested data-testid `diagnosis-target-${candidate}`, so one testid can appear several times on a page. The existing e2e assertions (`getByTestId("diagnosis-target-mcp")).toBeVisible()` in ui/e2e/smoke.spec.ts) pass only because each seeded target lands in exactly one cluster. On data where a target spans clusters, Playwright strict mode would fail. → In smoke.spec.ts, scope the target assertions to a cluster locator (clusters.filter(...).getByTestId(...)), or add a comment saying these testids are per-cluster and not unique.

low/spec-deviation scripts/seed-run.ts:52-66,340-350 — The spec mixes idSalt into seedIdBase(dbPath, startedAtMs, idSalt). The code mixes it into seededIds' leading entropy bytes instead, and adds a `startedAt` SeedOptions field the spec does not list. Both produce the intended result: distinct n1 ids, and the sweep stays the default run. → No code change needed. Record the startedAt addition, and why it exists (so the trials-1 run sorts oldest), in the phase notes or commit message.

results.title: Scorer health and matrix bands
results.summary: Added src/report/scorer-health.ts with collectBands and collectScorerHealth. buildReport now writes pairs[].band and a guarded scorer_health block, adds the methodology sentence, bumps REPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION to 8 and prints a "bands:" line plus "suspect:" lines. The Matrix view loads report.json, which falls back to today's single grid if it is missing or fails. With a banded report it splits rows into a discriminating section and two collapsed <details> sections (solved by every arm, failed by every arm) under a scorer-health banner. Also added the uniform-pass and uniform-fail evals to the cell-states seed, regenerated dev data, and added e2e tests, 16 unit tests and a concepts.md section. Typecheck, lint, the four spec test files, genericity, ui:build and all 34 e2e tests pass. One exception: the spec's dev-data "git diff --quiet" command cannot pass until the regenerated dev data is committed, which this stage may not do. Two regenerations gave the same tree hash, so the output is deterministic. In the full `bun test` run, one mcp-proxy test fails only because the Docker daemon is not running. — The implementation matches the Phase 3 spec. collectBands and collectScorerHealth in src/report/scorer-health.ts follow the band and suspect rules exactly: scored > 0 arms only, graded checks only, failed-by-all evals only, and a fixed summary template that interpolates no names. They are wired into buildReport with the language guard, the methodology sentence, the renderer lines, and REPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION 8. The Matrix band sections, the banner, the seed data, the regenerated dev data (the snapshot carries schema 8 and the uniform-fail suspect), the docs, and the tests all cover the specified cases, including (a)-(f), the five band cases, and the old-report fallback. The three findings are low-severity UX and wording notes, so it is ready to commit. I only read the code; I did not run the tests, typecheck, lint, or e2e.
findings: low/logic ui/src/views/Matrix.tsx:887-895 — When every eval is unbanded (e.g. a single-experiment run), the only section still reads "Discriminating (N evals) — arms disagree (N evals with one scored arm)", which claims the arms disagree when there is only one arm. The spec asked for this layout, so this is a wording issue, not a deviation. → When discriminatingRows.length === unbandedCount, drop the "— arms disagree" suffix (or use an "Unbanded" heading), and add an e2e/unit case for it

low/logic ui/src/views/Matrix.tsx:870-882 — The scorer-health banner lists every suspect in the run, ignoring the suite toggle and metadata filters. A filtered view can therefore name an eval that is not shown in any band. → Filter the suspects to eval ids in grid.rows, or note in the banner that it covers the whole run

low/spec-deviation ui/src/components/Heatmap.tsx:733 — The spec says the optional `band` prop labels "the header". The code only uses it in the region's aria-label, and the visible header is the <h4>/<summary> in Matrix.tsx. The result is fine for accessibility but does not match the spec's wording. → Leave the code as is and update the prop's doc comment to say it labels the scroll region for assistive tech
